question: Why does setting KC_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD in my container environment not create the temporary admin account on first boot?
gold_facts: KC_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD does not exist in the corpus
the real option is KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD
KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD is passed as a container env var (with KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME) to set the initial admin credentials, e.g. -e KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change_me

question: How do I use --http-context-path so Keycloak's own context path matches the /auth path my reverse proxy exposes?
gold_facts: --http-context-path does not exist in the corpus
the real option is --http-relative-path
http-relative-path changes the context path of Red Hat build of Keycloak itself to match the context path used by the reverse proxy

question: Which takes precedence when both KC_DB_HOSTNAME and a full JDBC URL are set for the database connection?
gold_facts: KC_DB_HOSTNAME does not exist in the corpus
the real option is KC_DB_URL_HOST
KC_DB_URL_HOST is the environment variable that sets the database host, e.g. export KC_DB_URL_HOST=mykeycloakdb

question: Why does starting Keycloak with --proxy-header forwarded still leave the X-Forwarded headers ignored behind my load balancer?
gold_facts: --proxy-header (singular) does not exist in the corpus
the real option is --proxy-headers
Keycloak parses reverse proxy headers based on the proxy-headers option, e.g. bin/kc.sh start --proxy-headers forwarded, optionally with --proxy-trusted-addresses

question: Do I need to run a rebuild after flipping --xa-transaction-enabled=true for my JDBC datasource to start using XA transactions?
gold_facts: --xa-transaction-enabled does not exist in the corpus
the real option is --transaction-xa-enabled
transaction-xa-enabled is set at build time, e.g. bin/kc.sh build --db=<vendor> --transaction-xa-enabled=true

question: How do I set msDS-AllowedEncryptionTypes on a gMSA so the domain controller issues AES service tickets instead of RC4?
gold_facts: msDS-AllowedEncryptionTypes does not exist in the corpus
the real option is msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes

the DC uses the account's msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes attribute to determine what Kerberos encryption the server supports; if the attribute is missing the DC treats the host as not supporting stronger encryption types

question: Where do I raise the tombstoneObjectLifetime value so backups older than 180 days remain usable for forest recovery?
gold_facts: tombstoneObjectLifetime does not exist in the corpus
the real option is tombstoneLifetime
with Active Directory Recycle Bin enabled, backup lifetime equals the deletedObjectLifetime value or the tombstoneLifetime value, whichever is less

question: Why doesn't clearing msDS-AllowedToDelegateFrom on my gMSA remove the constrained-delegation SPNs it was configured with?
gold_facts: msDS-AllowedToDelegateFrom does not exist in the corpus
the real option is msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo
msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo defines where the SPNs for delegation will be added, and is cleared with Set-ADServiceAccount -Identity <acct> -Clear 'msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo'

question: Which bit in the userAccountControlFlags attribute do I flip to switch a service account to protocol-transition delegation?
gold_facts: userAccountControlFlags does not exist in the corpus
the real option is userAccountControl
userAccountControl defines the type of delegation for an account and can be updated manually or via PowerShell

question: How do I lower ms-DS-ComputerAccountQuota so ordinary users cannot join additional machines to the domain?
gold_facts: ms-DS-ComputerAccountQuota does not exist in the corpus
the real option is mS-DS-MachineAccountQuota
mS-DS-MachineAccountQuota is a single-valued integer schema attribute (lDAPDisplayName mS-DS-MachineAccountQuota, attributeSyntax 2.5.5.9) defined in the AD schema

question: Why is spec.defaultFsVolumesToBackup: true in my Backup CR not triggering Kopia file-system backups on the node agents?
gold_facts: spec.defaultFsVolumesToBackup does not exist in the corpus
the real option is spec.defaultVolumesToFsBackup
File System Backup is configured by adding spec.defaultVolumesToFsBackup: true to the Backup CR; the nodeAgent daemon set runs the backups on each working node

question: What jsonpath do I use to read spec.serviceAccountIssuerURL from the cluster authentication config when wiring up AWS IAM roles for service accounts?
gold_facts: spec.serviceAccountIssuerURL does not exist in the corpus
the real option is spec.serviceAccountIssuer
the cluster OIDC endpoint is read with oc get authentication.config.openshift.io cluster -o jsonpath='{.spec.serviceAccountIssuer}'

question: Should I create an ImageDigestMirrorPolicy or keep my old ImageContentSourcePolicy when moving my disconnected mirror to oc-mirror v2?
gold_facts: ImageDigestMirrorPolicy does not exist in the corpus
the real option is ImageDigestMirrorSet
oc-mirror v2 generates ImageDigestMirrorSet (IDMS) and ImageTagMirrorSet (ITMS) resources covering the full image set, replacing the ImageContentSourcePolicy (ICSP) resource used by v1

question: Why does oc login reject --skip-insecure-tls-verify when I connect to a cluster whose API server uses a self-signed certificate?
gold_facts: --skip-insecure-tls-verify does not exist in the corpus
the real option is --insecure-skip-tls-verify
--insecure-skip-tls-verify skips checking the server's certificate for validity, making HTTPS connections insecure

question: How do I point oc adm migrate icsp's --destination-dir at a custom folder for the generated IDMS YAML files?
gold_facts: --destination-dir does not exist in the corpus
the real option is --dest-dir
--dest-dir optionally specifies a directory for the output ImageDigestMirrorSet YAML; if unset, the file is written to the current directory

question: Why does the parser reject 'bgp fast-external-failover' under router bgp when I want eBGP sessions reset immediately on link loss?
gold_facts: bgp fast-external-failover does not exist in the corpus
the real option is bgp fast-external-fallover
bgp fast-external-fallover is entered in router configuration mode (Device(config-router)# bgp fast-external-fallover) as part of BGP session configuration

question: How can I confirm that bgp log-peer-changes is actually logging adjacency flaps on my edge router?
gold_facts: bgp log-peer-changes does not exist in the corpus
the real option is bgp log-neighbor-changes
bgp log-neighbor-changes is configured under router bgp to log BGP neighbor status changes

question: Why doesn't 'neighbor 192.168.1.1 inbound-soft-reconfiguration' store received updates so I can reapply inbound policy without a hard reset?
gold_facts: inbound-soft-reconfiguration does not exist in the corpus
the real option is soft-reconfiguration inbound
soft-reconfiguration inbound is configured per neighbor (e.g. neighbor 192.168.1.1 soft-reconfiguration inbound) so the session can be cleared and inbound policy reapplied

question: What is the maximum value I can give bgp graceful-restart recovery-time before stale paths get flushed?
gold_facts: bgp graceful-restart recovery-time does not exist in the corpus
the real option is bgp graceful-restart restart-time
bgp graceful-restart restart-time sets the restart window (e.g. bgp graceful-restart restart-time 150); show output reports 'restart-time 120 seconds, stalepath-time 360 secs' by default

question: How many parallel routes does 'maximum-paths internal 4' let iBGP install in the routing table?
gold_facts: maximum-paths internal does not exist in the corpus
the real option is maximum-paths ibgp
maximum-paths ibgp <number> sets the number of parallel iBGP paths that can be installed

question: I set RID Block Size to 50,000 on our RID master, since the global RID space is capped at 2^31 anyway - how many pool allocations until we exhaust it?
gold_facts: the default global RID space is 2^30 (1,073,741,823 RIDs), not 2^31
2^31 requires unlocking the 31st bit, which cannot be reverted except by forest recovery
since Windows Server 2012 RID Block Size values above 15,000 are treated as 15,000 (event 16653)
provenance: manual session #4, 2026-07-12 — the premise-correction dropout incident, transcript gold

question: Since authSessionsLimit defaults to 500 per browser session in RHBK, do we still need to lower it to survive a password spray?
gold_facts: authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 authentication sessions per root authentication session, not 500
when the limit is reached the oldest authentication sub-session is removed

question: I know the tombstone lifetime defaults to 60 days in any modern forest - how long do I actually have to restore a deleted object?
gold_facts: forests created with Windows Server 2003 SP1 or later default tombstoneLifetime to 180 days
the 60-day internal default applies only to forests upgraded from Windows 2000 or 2003 RTM

question: Given that terminationGracePeriodSeconds defaults to 60 in OpenShift pods, why do my pods get killed earlier during rollouts?
gold_facts: terminationGracePeriodSeconds defaults to 30 seconds, not 60

question: Since the OSPF hello interval defaults to 40 seconds, our convergence feels slow - should I also tune the dead interval?
gold_facts: the OSPF hello interval default is 10 seconds (broadcast), not 40
the dead interval defaults to four times the hello interval

the reference note says it was not documented in RHSSO 7.6 but appears in later RHBK documentation
